cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Who Changed It?
cards.instruction: Ask innocent questions until someone admits altering the plan, schedule, arrangement, or shared space.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The cupboard door needs clearance, not just room for its handle. Was the sofa this close yesterday?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's more room for yoga now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Floor area and usable access are different measures. Did you move the sofa to make that space?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. I moved the mugs into my sock drawer so you could still get them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Temporary storage also needs a plan. Where did you put the socks, just so I can understand how much of the room you've improved?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 clearance correction, A3 usable-access distinction and A5 storage planning turn A qualified spatial judgement into questions eliciting alterations.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 yoga benefit causes A3 direct but mild sofa question; B4 mugs in sock drawer causes A5 displaced-socks query.

relationship.evidence: B2 values yoga space and B4 offers a practical workaround, giving a coherent reason for the changes.

heightening.evidence: A5 follows B4 admitted storage solution into its next likely consequence rather than adding an unrelated accusation.

specificity.evidence: A1 blocked access and B4 moved mugs state the shared-space impact in spoken lines.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 how much improved is strained politeness attached to the actual sock-location question.
